questions.q: What is the first real step after an alert from Lesson 23 fires?
options: A person confirms whether it's a real incident or a false positive, then decides how to act
A pause mechanism triggers automatically with no human involvement
The contract is immediately redeployed from scratch
The alert is ignored until the next scheduled review meeting
questions.explain: An alert firing starts a triage process -- confirming it's real and assessing urgency comes before any response action.

questions.q: Why does a full, timestamped alert history matter beyond just the most recent alert?
options: It lets a team reconstruct what actually happened, in what order, which becomes the raw material for a postmortem
It has no practical use once the immediate incident is resolved
It automatically generates the fix for whatever caused the incident
Only the single most recent alert is ever relevant to an investigation
questions.explain: A full history across time is what makes reconstructing an incident's actual sequence of events possible, feeding directly into Lesson 25's postmortem process.

questions.q: Why should alerts route to different destinations based on severity, rather than all going to the same place?
options: A routine check-in can go to email, while something needing an immediate human response needs to reach PagerDuty or an on-call rotation
All alerts should always go to the same destination regardless of urgency
Severity-based routing is only relevant for smart contract testing, not incident response
Email is always the correct destination for every kind of alert
questions.explain: Routing based on severity ensures urgent incidents reach someone who can respond immediately, while routine signals don't create unnecessary urgency.

questions.q: What does a pause mechanism (circuit breaker) actually accomplish during an incident?
options: It buys time by stopping new deposits/withdrawals while the team investigates -- it does not fix the underlying problem
It automatically reverses all transactions that already occurred before the pause
It permanently fixes the vulnerability that caused the incident
It has no effect on ongoing contract activity
questions.explain: A pause stops new activity going forward; it buys investigation time rather than resolving the root cause, and cannot undo funds already moved.

questions.q: Why does this lesson argue pause authority shouldn't rest with a single engineer's key, referencing Chapter 3, Lesson 16?
options: A single key holding that much power is itself a risk, the same reasoning behind multisig-controlled deployments
Single-key pause authority is actually the recommended best practice
Multisig wallets cannot be used for pause functions, only for deployments
Pause authority has nothing to do with deployment key management
questions.explain: The same logic that favors multisig-controlled deployments applies to pause authority -- concentrating that much power in one key is a risk in itself.
